To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the content, composition and functional properties of wheat proteins can be manipulated by using genetic, agronomic or technological methods, and that this can be used to reduce the exposure of susceptible individuals to gluten and/or its immunogenic peptides.
the use of wheat proteins in the formulation of foods for coeliac patients is limited due to the presence of gluten proteins, which can cause intestinal damage.
the use of wheat protein isolates and gluten free commodities can reduce the exposure to wheat proteins in coeliac disease patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of strategies that will enable the production of wheat varieties with reduced levels of potentially harmful proteins and with the development of technologies to reduce the exposure of susceptible individuals to these proteins.
improving our understanding of the structure and function of the wheat seed proteins, and with developing strategies that will allow the production of safe wheat-based foods.

the study of the effects of genetic, environmental, and technological factors on the content, composition and functional properties of wheat proteins and gluten, and with the development of strategies for the reduction of adverse reactions in susceptible individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many ways to modify the wheat grain, and the resulting products, but none of these are yet sufficiently effective to provide a solution for the coeliac disease patient.
wheat proteins, especially gluten proteins, have a very important nutritional role and that their consumption is safe for the great majority of individuals.
the use of gluten in food products is safe for the general population, but not for coeliac patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of new wheat varieties with lower gluten contents and/or improved technological properties, and the use of gluten isolates in the food industry, are promising strategies to reduce the exposure of sensitive individuals to gluten proteins and/or their immunogenic peptides.
the content and composition of wheat gluten proteins can be modulated through breeding or genetic modification, and the use of these proteins as food ingredients can be improved by using isolates.

the use of wheat proteins in food systems is not always beneficial for the consumer, but the development of novel strategies to manipulate their content and composition could help in the design of safe and nutritious foods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of gluten in the food industry can be optimized by using appropriate technologies and/or by selecting wheat cultivars with reduced levels of gluten proteins.

, while it is possible to produce wheat with a low content of gluten and/or amylase trypsins inhibitors, the technological and nutritional properties of such wheat will be significantly altered, which may not be acceptable to consumers.
the use of wheat protein isolates, especially those obtained from wheat cultivars with low gluten contents, may be an alternative to gluten-free diets in coeliac patients.
